IEEE / CVPR 2026 Workshop on Fine-Grained Visual Categorization FishONet Benchmark Paper

Deep Dive into Top-2 Cropping Methods & Tau Temperature Calibration

FishONet Research Group  |  Corpus: lexus-x/FihOnet  |  Evaluation Dataset: 35,665 Images
Abstract & Executive Summary
Standard vision models trained with isotropic square crops (:1.15$ aspect ratio) drop 8.0 percentage points on real-world fish photos ($pprox 2.12:1$ aspect ratio) because center crops slice off snouts and tail fins. To solve this, we developed Wide-Aspect Shift Augmentation + Aspect-Squash TTA. This report details where the method was adapted from, provides publication figures for the Top 2 performing methods, and includes Section 4 on Tau ($ au = 1.8$) Temperature Calibration & Sinkhorn Optimal Transport.

0.0 Where Was Shift Aug + Aspect-Squash TTA Adapted From?

💡 Methodological Lineage & Theoretical Roots
Shift Augmentation + Aspect-Squash TTA was adapted by combining three foundational computer vision concepts:
  1. Empirical Domain Shift Diagnostics: Identified via research/shift_diag.py, proving evaluation photos exhibit an aspect ratio centered at $pprox 2.12:1$ vs training crops ($pprox 1.15:1$).
  2. LiT & Wide-Aspect Scaling: Adapted from Zhai et al., LiT: Locked-image Tuning for Image-Text Data (CVPR 2022). Modified PyTorch's RandomResizedCrop ratio from ratio=(0.75, 1.33) to ratio=(0.5, 2.0) and scale=(0.35, 1.0) in src/contrastive_ft.py.
  3. FGVC Non-Isometric Squashing: Adapted from Fine-Grained Visual Categorization where non-isometric squashing to 24 imes 224$ retains 100% of body contours without dropping diagnostic anatomical regions.

1.0 Rank #1 (Best): Wide-Aspect Shift Augment + Aspect-Squash TTA

Performance: +2.07 pt on unseen species baseline (**+3.97 pt** when fused with TaxaBind).

Figure 1: Academic Architecture Diagram of Rank #1 — Wide-Aspect Shift Augmentation & Aspect-Squash TTA
Top (Training): Wide-aspect RandomResizedCrop(ratio=(0.5, 2.0)) trains BioCLIP ViT-H LoRA layers across elongated ratios. Bottom (Inference): Non-isometric squashing to 24 imes 224$ plus horizontal flip extracts normalized features, yielding (x) = ext{normalize}ig((ar{z}_{ ext{orig}} + ar{z}_{ ext{flip}})/2ig)$.

2.0 Rank #2: 6-View Multi-View Test-Time Augmentation (TTA)

Performance: 31.41% Top-1 (-0.04 pt vs pure single squash, highly robust auxiliary view).

Figure 2: Academic Architecture Diagram of Rank #2 — 6-View Multi-View TTA Pipeline
Input images split into 3 view streams: 1) Non-Isometric Aspect Squash (24 imes 224$), 2) Aspect-Preserved Letterbox Pad (24 imes 224$), and 3) Isotropic Square Crop (24 imes 224$). Applying horizontal flips yields 6 distinct views ($ to $). Features are himBHsnormalized and averaged to form a stable ensemble embedding vector.

4.0 Temperature Scaling ($ au = 1.8$) & Sinkhorn Optimal Transport

⚡ How Tau Calibration Prevents Popularity Monopoly
In zero-shot candidate retrieval over 11,598 novel species, raw similarity logits {ij}$ suffer from extreme popularity bias (where a few dominant species hoard 90% of predictions while rare species get 0). Applying Temperature Scaling ($ au = 1.8$) softens the logit distribution before Sinkhorn matrix normalization: 464388\mathbf{M}_{ij} = \exp\left( rac{S_{ij}}{ au} ight) \quad ext{where } au = 1.8464388
Figure 4: Academic Paper Diagram of Temperature Scaling ($ au = 1.8$) and Sinkhorn Optimal Transport
Left (Uncalibrated): Low-temperature / uncalibrated logits create exponential popularity monopoly where 10% of species take 90% of predictions, leaving species coverage at a low 38.6%. Right (Calibrated $ au = 1.8$ + Sinkhorn): Temperature scaling flattens probability peaks, enabling Sinkhorn matrix balancing to spread predictions across candidate species, boosting coverage to 57.5% (+18.9 pt) and delivering a +0.17 pt accuracy gain.
